concepts.title: Naming Aldehydes and Ketones in Both Systems
concepts.definition: Common aldehyde names swap the -ic of the parent acid for aldehyde and mark positions with Greek letters, while IUPAC names end in -al counted from the aldehyde carbon itself; ketones name their two groups around the C=O in common usage but take -one with lowest-locant numbering in IUPAC.
concepts.key_idea: When CHO hangs on a ring the suffix carbaldehyde follows the cycloalkane name, and benzaldehyde is the accepted parent for aromatic members.
question_patterns: write the IUPAC name of CH3CH(CH3)CH2CH2CHO

solution_steps.action: find the parent chain through the carbonyl carbon
solution_steps.explain: aldehydes force the CHO carbon to be C-1; ketones number from the nearer end
ring-bound CHO takes carbaldehyde, and common names survive for acetone, acetophenone and benzaldehyde

concepts.title: Preparation Routes to Aldehydes and Ketones
concepts.definition: Primary alcohols yield aldehydes on controlled oxidation or dehydrogenation over hot copper or silver, secondary alcohols give ketones, alkenes cleave to carbonyls by ozonolysis with zinc and water, and only ethyne hydrates to an aldehyde while every other alkyne lands on a ketone with Hg2+ and acid.
concepts.key_idea: Aldehyde synthesis leans on stopping oxidations one rung early: PCC, Rosenmund reduction of acyl chlorides, Stephen or DIBAL-H on nitriles, Etard or side-chain chlorination on toluene, and Gatterman-Koch formylation for ring-bound CHO.

concepts.title: Ketones from Acyl Chlorides, Nitriles and Friedel-Crafts Acylation
concepts.definition: Dialkylcadmium, built from cadmium chloride and a Grignard reagent, couples with acyl chlorides to ketones; a nitrile attacked by a Grignard reagent hydrolyses to a ketone; and benzene plus an acid chloride over anhydrous AlCl3 delivers aryl ketones by Friedel-Crafts acylation.
concepts.key_idea: Cadmium reagents are softer than Grignards, so they stop at the ketone instead of racing on to tertiary alcohols.

solution_steps.explain: R2Cd adds once to RCOCl stopping at the ketone; RMgX adds to nitriles giving an imine salt that hydrolyses to C=O

solution_steps.action: use the Lewis acid for arene routes
solution_steps.explain: anhydrous AlCl3 generates the acylium ion that substitutes the ring in Friedel-Crafts acylation

concepts.title: Boiling Points and Solubility across Carbonyls and Acids
concepts.definition: Dipole-dipole forces put aldehydes and ketones above hydrocarbons and ethers of matching mass but below alcohols, and carboxylic acids boil higher still because paired molecules stay hydrogen-bonded even as dimers in the vapour; water solubility fades as the hydrophobic chain grows.
concepts.formula: bp_order_same_mass = alkane < ether < aldehyde < alcohol < acid
concepts.key_idea: Lower members such as methanal and ethanoic acid mix with water in any ratio thanks to hydrogen bonding, while benzoic acid barely dissolves in cold water.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech203.txt section 8.3 with Example 8.2 and section 8.8 (lines ~454-526, ~1140-1162)
question_patterns: account for dimer formation by carboxylic acid molecules in the vapour phase

solution_steps.explain: dispersion only, then dipole-dipole, then hydrogen bonding decides the boiling ladder

solution_steps.action: weigh hydrophobic bulk against water bonding
solution_steps.explain: small carbonyls and acids hydrogen-bond into water; long chains and benzene rings shut it out

concepts.title: Nucleophilic Addition and Carbonyl Reactivity Order
concepts.definition: The polar C=O invites nucleophiles: attack from above or below the sp2 plane flips carbon to sp3 in a tetrahedral alkoxide that then grabs a proton; aldehydes out-react ketones because one small hydrogen beats two bulky, electron-pushing groups, and resonance-cushioned aryl carbonyls are slower still.
concepts.key_idea: Base speeds the HCN addition by feeding cyanide ions, and bisulphite addition crystallises aldehydes cleanly since the equilibrium sits right for them but left for ketones.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech203.txt section 8.4.1 with Fig 8.2 and Example 8.3 (lines ~530-635)

solution_steps.explain: fewer, smaller substituents leave the carbonyl carbon more exposed and more positive

solution_steps.explain: nucleophile adds first making an alkoxide, then solvent protonates to the neutral addition product

concepts.title: Acetals, Ketals and Ammonia Derivatives of C=O
concepts.definition: One alcohol molecule gives a hemiacetal and a second gives a gem-dialkoxy acetal under dry HCl, ethylene glycol closes cyclic ketals, and H2N-Z reagents condense to C=N derivatives: hydroxylamine gives oximes, hydrazine hydrazones, and 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine the coloured solids used to characterise carbonyls.
concepts.key_idea: Acetals survive base but hydrolyse back to the carbonyl in aqueous mineral acid, which makes them handy protecting groups.

solution_steps.action: count the alcohol equivalents for acetals
solution_steps.explain: two alcohol molecules (or one diol) replace both carbonyl oxygens' role, water leaves each time

concepts.title: Reductions to Alcohols and to Methylene
concepts.definition: NaBH4, LiAlH4 or catalytic hydrogenation drop aldehydes to primary and ketones to secondary alcohols, while Clemmensen (Zn-Hg with concentrated HCl) and Wolff-Kishner (hydrazine then hot alkali in a high-boiling solvent) strip the oxygen entirely, turning C=O into CH2.
concepts.key_idea: Choose the medium by functional-group tolerance: acid-stable substrates take Clemmensen, base-stable ones take Wolff-Kishner.

solution_steps.explain: hydride or hydrogenation stops at the alcohol; Clemmensen or Wolff-Kishner digs down to CH2

concepts.title: Tollens and Fehling Tests to Catch Aldehydes
concepts.definition: Mild oxidants separate aldehydes from ketones: warming with ammoniacal silver nitrate plates a bright silver mirror, and Fehling's A-B mixture throws a reddish brown precipitate on heating with an aliphatic aldehyde, both oxidising the aldehyde to its carboxylate while ketones sit still.
concepts.key_idea: Aromatic aldehydes pass Tollens but fail Fehling, so the two tests together also separate aliphatic from aromatic aldehydes.

concepts.title: Haloform Reaction Carbon Accounting
concepts.definition: Methyl ketones oxidised by sodium hypohalite lose their methyl group as haloform, so the sodium carboxylate that survives carries exactly one carbon fewer than the starting carbonyl compound.
concepts.key_idea: A positive iodoform test flags any CH3CO- group (or a CH3CH(OH)- that oxidises to one), and the C=C of an unsaturated ketone survives the reaction untouched.

concepts.title: Alpha-Hydrogen Chemistry: Aldol versus Cannizzaro
concepts.definition: Carbonyls owning at least one alpha hydrogen enolise under dilute alkali and couple into beta-hydroxy aldehydes or ketols that dehydrate to alpha,beta-unsaturated products (aldol condensation), while aldehydes stripped of alpha hydrogens instead disproportionate in concentrated alkali, one molecule becoming an alcohol and another an acid salt (Cannizzaro).
concepts.key_idea: Cross aldol between two different enolisable partners scatters four products, which is why it is planned only when one partner cannot enolise.

concepts.title: Naming Carboxylic Acids and the Carboxyl Structure
concepts.definition: IUPAC names swap the alkane -e for -oic acid counting the carboxyl carbon as C-1, multiply with dicarboxylic or tricarboxylic acid markers, and ring acids use carboxylic acid or benzoic acid; the carboxyl carbon itself is less electrophilic than a plain carbonyl because resonance shares the charge with the hydroxyl oxygen.
concepts.key_idea: Common names remember sources: formic from ants, acetic from vinegar, butyric from rancid butter.

concepts.title: Ascending the Series by One Carbon
concepts.definition: Both carbonation routes climb one rung: a Grignard reagent poured onto dry ice adds the carboxyl carbon, and a nitrile hydrolysis keeps the new carbon too, so an alkyl halide of n carbons becomes an acid of n+1 carbons; the first hop swaps the halide for magnesium without changing the count.
concepts.key_idea: Nitriles themselves come from alkyl halides plus cyanide, which is exactly the extra carbon that hydrolysis later reveals as COOH.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech203.txt sections 8.7(3)-(4), nitrile hydrolysis and Grignard carbonation (lines ~1063-1082)

concepts.title: Acidity of Carboxylic Acids and Substituent Effects
concepts.definition: Two equivalent resonance structures park the negative charge on oxygens in the carboxylate ion, so carboxylic acids beat phenols and alcohols in acidity; electron-withdrawing substituents strengthen the acid and electron donors weaken it, and effervescence with bicarbonate unmasks the COOH group.
concepts.formula: ewg_order_acidity = ph < i < br < cl < f < cn < no2 < cf3
concepts.key_idea: Trifluoroacetic acid tops the family while formic acid beats acetic, and distance matters: alpha chlorine helps far more than gamma chlorine.
concepts.textbook_ref: lech203.txt section 8.9.1 with Ka data and Intext 8.8 (lines ~1163-1273)

concepts.title: Reactions of the Carboxyl Group: Esters, Acyl Chlorides, Amides, Reduction and Decarboxylation
concepts.definition: The OH side of COOH swaps partners readily: mineral acid esterifies with alcohols (water must leave to push equilibrium), PCl5 or SOCl2 installs chlorine, ammonia first salts then heats to an amide; LiAlH4 or diborane reduces the whole group to a primary alcohol, and soda-lime decarboxylation or Kolbe electrolysis of salts clips or doubles the carbon skeleton.
concepts.key_idea: Diborane is the gentler reducer because it leaves esters, nitro and halo groups alone, and NaBH4 cannot touch the carboxyl group at all.

solution_steps.explain: acid-catalysed esterification, PCl5 or SOCl2 substitution, and ammonium salt dehydration each rewrite the C-OH bond
